verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly has a dedicated, documented 'Scheduled flag changes' feature that lets users define changes to a flag's targeting rules for future points in time. It also supports expiration dates for flag targeting, which is a related one-off time-bound change. missing for 10: explicit evidence that scheduling applies to broader releases (such as starting a progressive or guarded rollout at a set time), detail on schedule mechanics like time zones, API or CLI scheduling, and approvals of scheduled changes, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can schedule flag changes and releases to happen at a specific future time

citations.quote: Scheduling flag changes lets you define and schedule changes to your flag's targeting rules for future points in time.
You can even set expiration dates for flag targeting if you know you only want customers to receive a flag for a specific period of time.
